Skill created. The genuinely generalizable lessons from this question were:

1. **Retrospective multi-year monthly tables in mid-year bulletins** — the June 1970 bulletin contains the full 1960-1969 monthly yield history in one table, so you don't hunt across ten bulletins. The window almost always ends just before the publication date.
2. **Where the yield/interest-rate tables live** and which series columns appear together (Treasury bonds, Corporate Aaa/Aa/A/Baa, municipals).
3. **Per-month-spread-then-mean** ordering, with the exact-rating and exact-maturity matching pitfalls.
4. **"N significant digits" ≠ N decimal places.**

I saved these as `research/officeqa-bond-yield-spread-monthly` and cross-linked it against the existing AA-corporate-regression memory note so a future agent won't confuse the simple spread question with the forecasting trap.

No memory update needed — these facts are procedural and live better in the skill than in the compact (98%-full) memory store.
